Replying to @naomi when pricing my pieces I consider time spent making/decorating/signing/waxing/glazing/sanding/lustering/firing/invetorying. I have done time studies to help gauge the time I spend on making the pieces. I also consider materials used. I apply gold luster to almost every piece and it’s expensive and requires an additional firing which is also another expense. I also consider experience. I have been working with clay for 14 years now so I consider all of those years of working to this point in my pieces value as well. Pricing is hard! Placing a value on your art is uncomfortable. I’m just happy to be here and I’m doing my best with the knowledge I have gained so far on this journey. I don’t think there is a right answer that will work for everyone, I’m just trying to do what feels right to me! Thank you for reading! 💗💗💗💗 #wheelthrown #ceramics #sliptrailing #potterytiktok #porcelain

Pottery thrown and fired the same day is possible and heres how. There are so many exciting changes happening in pottery at the moment and this Small wheel from @Small Ceramics is a real game changer for learning, speed and cuteness! In this video I throw, bisque and then glaze my pottery in the microwave, its fast and helps me learn throwing and glazing techniques quickly -you can do bisque , earthenware and stoneware but I love Raku firing which im doing here, This form of western Raku uses a copper heavy glaze called copper penny. In reduction (no oxygen) it turns metallic which you can see happen in the video, then when its re exposed to oxygen it turns lustrous in a whole range of colours and rainbows. I will be demonstrating small throwing at Potfest in Glynde (and maybe Microwave firing too weather permitting, ) so come and say hi, have a go and help celebrate a small but massively exciting way that pottery is getting more accessible and affordable. If your a potter or have any questions about clay, glazes,bisque, raku, earthenware or stoneware firings write them below and I will make sure I compile a list of answers 👇 #potterytiktok #potteryvids #wheelthrowing #clay #raku

In my YouTube video this weekend I’m recreating some pots I haven’t thrown since 2014, specially store jars with inset, internal galleries and thin lids with thrown knobs. You can find a link to the fully narrated video via the Linktree in my profile’s biography.   I’ve lied a little bit. I did create jars that were similar to this during my apprenticeship with Lisa Hammond between 2014-2017, yet they were bellied pieces with a gallery closer to the jars I make these days, yet they unusual thrown knobs that were in themselves similar to small bowls.   To create pots with internal galleries like this you need to split the rim. One section becomes the lip, the other is coaxed inside and carefully set horizontal to essentially become a ledge onto which the lid can be held aloft. This alone is a tricky task and it involves throwing a form with enough material in the lip to withstand such a manoeuvre. Secondly, there’s the small disc-like lid, a form that’s thrown off-the-hump and then the following day it’s trimmed back to have its more exacting shape and the knob is thrown on, again, a tricky task as it involves fiddly, fingertip throwing and a lot of accuracy.   All of this and more will be covered in my longer, narrated YouTube upload. I enjoyed making these and since it has been such a long time since I’ve crafted them, my skillset in the interim has improved massively, thus I could apply newly learnt techniques and ability into making shapes I used to struggle with to some degree. I hope you like the film if you happen to click over and watch it, it’s greatly appreciated if you do as it helps to keep the lights on in the workshop.   #pottery #ceramics #handmade #jar #satisfying

I’m a sucker for the making of pots, the joyous throwing and trimming, but what comes after, the waxing, glazing and firing, is more of a laborious task that normally ends up being highly repetitive. I don’t mind the work, I keep my headphones on and listen to stories throughout the day, yet I definitely experience more pain in my hands from these processes, as compared to throwing and trimming. Specifically, it’s the grasping of pots as I fettle the surface clean, as the fingers that are gripped so tightly around the object cannot move, otherwise they rub down the surface and create thin patches that show in the finished pots. This means that the hand that holds the pots is tensed for hours on end with my fingers pressed against a relatively powdery surface, if I squeeze too hard, the clay can fracture and come off of the vessel and too loose a grip means my digits glide across the surface, again creating thin spots. It’s hard to describe, but essentially this hand becomes a vice whilst the other carefully cleans the surface. It’s a skill, just like any other in the making process. #pottery #glazing #glaze #howto #craftsmanship #ceramics

If you’d like to see a far more thorough exploration of these vases, I recommend watching the 40-minute version that’s on my YouTube channel, a link to which you can find via the Linktree in my profile’s biography.   This week I’m making some of my favourite pots, they aren’t really about function, at least that is not what I’m thinking about whilst I create them. These angular vases with a protruding line across one side are simple, decorative objects and a welcome change after a few weeks of focusing solely on functional ware. I take my time with them and pay close attention to proportion and surface and how the line travels and over the past few years they’ve changed quite a lot.   They used to appear squatter and the lines were heavier and less defined but after making many batches, they have gradually become taller and more refined, in my opinion. The carved line has followed that shift, it’s sharper now, more deliberate and despite only being a relatively small addition, the change it makes is drastic. Most of my work is thrown on the wheel and naturally symmetrical and therefore this detail interrupts that uniformity. It gives the vessel a direction and a front. It catches the light and throws a shadow across the flat planes and somehow that single line makes the pots feel more figurative, especially when they are grouped together.   If you happen to click over and watch the longer edition, thank you, it means so much!   #pottery #vase #sculpture #handmade #ceramics
